summary: Verifier re-score: 7.0/10, NOT on par (score < 7.5; no blocker open). odrum.glb sha 208d570f is the current shipped GLB. Both majors were reproduced. Splash M1 is confirmed and is stronger than written: the second jar, beside the mask, shows a blue ring around an orange centre and also reads as an eye, so the card carries two eye-like discs next to a pale scowling plate (_harness/_shots/closing_odrum_verify_splash_head.png). Icon M2 is confirmed. The eye recesses re-measure at p50 L* 13.0 / 2.0 (min 1.4) with sharp on art/out/fighters/odrum/icon.png, against the brief's own rule at _design/fighters/odrum.md:85 ('L* ~30 walls to ~21 floor ... never black holes'). At 48 px it reads stern, not horror, so it stays major and does not become a blocker. Re-running art/tools/clip_steps.py with Blender's bundled python reproduced the animation pops exactly: ult x_pot_l 1.902 m at f35, attack2 0.923 m, victory hand.L 0.543 m, cast_a1 1.157 m, channel 0.000 m (_harness/_reports/closing_odrum_verify_clip_steps.txt). The lineup and yoke numbers match the json. No missed sensitivity blocker: the cap is a low dome, the base mask has carved brow, nose keel and umber recesses at portrait size, and Shadeprint keeps its honey-amber inlays (ruling 2). Timing not_measured (load 85-147).

gapStatus.evidence: closing_odrum_game0_lab.txt: mask #EFC88F sat 0.40, jar #C5A271 sat 0.43 in the live frame (_harness/_shots/closing_odrum_game0_x4.png). Cards still show the mask pale cream (portrait.png, splash.png, noon_fair splash), which is covered by M1.
Cap #D5C9B6 sat 0.15, chest #AD9C8A sat 0.20 in game.
art/renders/fighters/odrum/three_odrum_shadeprint.png bottom row: upper coat and sleeves render near-white grey over a dark skirt, the pale-robe read.
art/renders/lineup/fw_CW6_m_lineup.json odrum: f0 57.6/51.0/30.6, f180 49.7/36.1/32.9, valueGradientOk false, accentOk false.
Load averages 85 / 147 / 114 at 15:03 (uptime), so the < 3 bar cannot be met.

findings.title: Base splash: the near jar reads as a giant eyeball and the figure is a washed, posterized cut-out
findings.what: The raised near jar is the largest shape on the card: a pale peach sphere, about 330 px across, with a single brown end-on disc, which reads as an eyeball. The verifier also sees the second jar, next to the mask, as a blue ring around an orange centre, a second eye-like disc beside the face. The figure is pale from mask to skirt, posterize streaks on the arms and chest read as wrappings, and the yoke is cropped to a stub. The base portrait and the Noon Fair splash show the same pale-cream mask rather than the in-game ochre.
findings.gauge: In a LoL splash the signature prop reads clearly and value structure carries the figure. No prop becomes an ambiguous organic shape.
findings.fix: Re-stage the base splash in Odrum's own Amber Hour throw. Run the yoke as a long diagonal, with both jars in three-quarter view showing glaze band, resin lip and lit window. Keep no jar nearer the lens than the head. Hold the figure at 60-70% of frame height. Grade the jerkin and trousers to their brief values and the mask to its in-game ochre. Re-run card_qa.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced by eye on the full card and the crop. Not raised to blocker: the mask has carved features and brown (not black) recesses at splash size, and the eye-like props are jars on a fighter, not a Wick face. Still, the jar/eyeball read next to a pale plate face pushes the card toward the horror line, so it should be fixed first.

findings.title: Icon eye recesses render as black holes, so the plate reads menacing at HUD size
findings.what: In the 128 px icon the almond recesses fall to near-black. With the cracked pale plate and the hard angled brow, the chip reads as a hollow-eyed scowl. The portrait keeps L* 26-29.
findings.evidence: art/out/fighters/odrum/icon.png re-measured with sharp: box 37,57,6,3 p50 L* 13.0; box 66,57,8,3 p50 L* 2.0, min 1.4. 48 px view: _harness/_shots/closing_odrum_verify_icon48.png. The rule is at _design/fighters/odrum.md:85; precedent is owner ruling 2 (hollow eye slits read blank or menacing).
findings.gauge: LoL face chips keep a readable, alive eye area at 48-64 px, even on masked champions.
findings.fix: Add a low warm fill from the jar side so the recess walls hold L* 25-30 and the floor stays at or above 18, with a small amber glint per recess. Ease the brow angle for the chip camera only. Check at 48 and 64 px.
findings.verifierNote: Measurement reproduced exactly. At 48 px it reads stern rather than horror, so it stays major. It breaks the fighter's own brief and the ruling-2 precedent, and the icon is the most-seen face in the HUD.

findings.title: One-frame jar and hand pops at the release of the ult, the autos, cast_a1 and victory
findings.what: Positional jumps within one 60 Hz frame: ult x_pot_l 1.902 m at f35 (clip 17.5), attack2 x_pot_l 0.923 m, cast_a1 x_pot_l 1.157 m, victory hand.L 0.543 m.
findings.evidence: Re-run: Blender python art/tools/clip_steps.py art/out/fighters/odrum/odrum.glb --clip <c> --nodes hand.L,hand.R,head,x_pot_l,x_pot_r --limit 0.15 -> _harness/_reports/closing_odrum_verify_clip_steps.txt
findings.gauge: Fast LoL whips keep continuous arcs (smear or stretch frames plus a trail), never a teleport.
findings.fix: Add in-betweens on the arc at the ult f17, attack2 f5 and cast_a1 f9. Spread victory's hand.L over 6 or more frames. Let the amber trail carry the speed.
findings.verifierNote: Numbers reproduced to the millimetre. Kept minor: these are one-frame release pops under VFX, not broken loops. The ult pop is close to major.

findings.title: Channel clip is frozen and carries the bar square
findings.what: Channel hand steps are 0.000 m and yoke yaw is 0 deg, so the bar reverts square across the shoulders.
findings.gauge: LoL channel and recall loops stay alive and keep the silhouette identity.
findings.fix: Rebuild the channel from the diagonal carry: a slow foot-to-foot sway, a small bar bob and a jar settle.

findings.title: Diagonal carry drops the near jar and its window low; lineup top band falls
findings.what: At facing 0 the accent top-half share is 0.234 and the top band 57.6. At facing 180 the bands are 49.7/36.1/32.9. Both valueGradientOk and accentOk are false.
findings.gauge: A champion's signature glow stays in the upper body at every facing.
findings.fix: Raise the low end of the carry or shorten its cord so the near jar hangs at hip height or above. Put the window on the upper belly of the jar facing the camera. Re-run lineup_qa.
findings.verifierNote: JSON values match. Minor: the in-match read is good (closing_odrum_game0_x4.png).

findings.title: Signature hue is weak against the lane: separation is by value only
findings.what: The cap (sat 0.15), the chest (sat 0.20, hue 31) and the skirt (hue 24) sit in the RIFT road's hue family (hue 33). The ochre is limited to the mask and the jars.
findings.evidence: _harness/_reports/closing_odrum_game0_lab.txt; _harness/_shots/closing_odrum_game0_x4.png (the cap and coat read white-grey in game).
findings.gauge: LoL champions own a readable signature hue at the gameplay camera, besides value contrast.
findings.fix: Spend more area on ochre within the 40% saturation rule (cap band, strap leather, jar glaze), and keep the jerkin cool walnut.

findings.title: Skin splashes are small cut-outs pasted on a blurred, re-used plate
findings.what: In the Noon Fair splash the figure takes about 65% of the height, pinned right, with no interaction with the scene and no ground contact shadow. It reads as a render on a backdrop. Its mask is also pale cream, not ochre.
findings.gauge: LoL skin splashes are bespoke compositions, with the figure lit by and integrated into its scene.
findings.fix: Ground the figure (contact shadow, matched rim light from the plate's key) and give each skin its own staging pose, with the yoke on a diagonal.
findings.verifierNote: Added by the verifier. The reviewer called these serviceable in its prose but did not list them. This is likely a roster-wide card pipeline issue, so it is kept minor here.
